details: Any of the about 250 species of flowering plant of the genus Nepeta, family Lamiaceae, certain of which are said to have medicinal qualities. Nepeta cataria and Nepeta grandiflora (and perhaps other species), which are well-known for causing an apparently harmless pheromone-based intoxication among certain cats.
A legendary creature from Ethiopia, said to have the body of a Cape buffalo, scales on its back, and the head of a wild boar, which always points downward because of its weight.
Any of the sharks in the family Scyliorhinidae
The killing of a cat, the slaughter of cats.
(US, historically, Yorkshire, Lincolnshire) Any of several perennial herbs, of the genus Typha, that have long flat leaves, and grow in marshy places.
Certain other livestock, such as sheep, pigs or goats. Also rarely applied to horses. (pejorative, figuratively) People who resemble domesticated bovine animals in behavior or destiny.
A small egret, Bubulcus ibis, of the heron family (Ardeidae)
A grid of parallel metal bars set into a road as an obstacle to prevent hooved animals from passing.
A stick designed to goad cows, steers, and similar animals in order to prompt them to move in a desired direction, now usually electrified to administer a stimulating shock to the animal.
A man who raises or tends cattle, as:
(botany) Any plant of the genus Cattleya, a genus of orchids.
(informal, of a person or remark) With subtle hostility in an effort to hurt, annoy, or upset, particularly among women. (informal) Resembling or characteristic of a cat.
(fashion) A narrow elevated stage on which models parade.
A grouping of all the members of a legislature from the same party.

(US, idiomatic) The competitive process in which a political party selects their candidate, especially presidential; a primary election via caucus. (US, idiomatic) A political competition; the game of campaigning and one-upmanship to get votes and be elected.
(zoology) Pertaining to the tail or posterior or hind part of a body.
The tailfin of a fish and other aquatic vertebrates.
(neuroanatomy) a nucleus within each hemisphere of the brain, sitting astride the thalamus and located near the center of the brain.
A military dictator, especially one ruling in Spain, Portugal or Latin America.
A specific government of a caudillo.
(idiomatic) Caught off guard, unprepared, or in an embarrassing situation.
The thin membrane which covers the lower intestines; the omentum. [from 14th c.]
The fatty, transparent serous membrane that covers the intestines of cows, sheep, and pigs, often used as a casing for sausages and other meat dishes.
A large bowl-shaped pot used for boiling over an open flame.
Any seaweed of the genus Caulerpa.
Brassica oleracea var. botrytis, an annual variety of cabbage, of which the cluster of young flower stalks and buds is eaten as a vegetable. The edible head or curd of a cauliflower plant.
(botany) Growing immediately on a caulis, the main stem of a plant; of or pertaining to a caulis.
To apply caulking to joints, cracks, or a juncture of different materials.
A person who caulks various structures (as ships) and certain types of piping.
A sealing material used to seal joints between heterogeneous materials in many kinds of construction and manufacture.
of, relating to, or being a cause of something; causing
(philosophy) The doctrine that actions have a direct cause, especially that people's actions are caused by their mental state at the time
The agency of a cause; the action or power of a cause, in producing its effect.
The act of causing.
Acting as a cause#Noun.

(countable, often with of, typically of adverse results) The source of, or reason for, an event or action; that which produces or effects a result. (countable) A goal, aim or principle, especially one which transcends purely selfish ends.
(transitive) To set off an event or action; to bring about; to produce. (ditransitive) To actively produce as a result, by means of force or authority.
(intransitive) To cause controversy, or raise a disturbance.
Causation; causality; the process whereby a cause leads to an effect.
(chiefly, UK) An issue or incident (originally, a legal case) arousing widespread controversy or public debate.
The official cause of a human death as typically determined by a coroner during an autopsy and included on the death certificate of a deceased person.

A road that is raised so as to be above water, marshland, and similar low-lying obstacles, which in some cases may flood periodically (e.g. due to tides). Originally causeways were much like dykes, generally pierced to let water through, whereas many modern causeways are more like bridges or viaducts.
Capable of burning, corroding or destroying organic tissue.
sodium hydroxide (NaOH), a strong alkaline substance used in the manufacture of paint, soap and detergents, or as a drain cleaner.
The quality of being physically caustic; burning, corrosive.
The act of searing organic tissue by the application of a cautery or caustic; also, the effect of such application.
To burn and hence seal open tissue using a heated article or caustic agent so as to stop bleeding or minimise the risk of infection.

Prudence when faced with, or when expecting to face, danger; care taken in order to avoid risk or harm. A careful attention to the probable effects of an act, in order that failure or harm may be avoided. Security; guaranty; bail.
(transitive) To warn; to alert, advise that caution is warranted.
Warning, often in the form of a sign, that people should pay attention when walking on a wet and slippery floor not to fall down and get injured.
Serving to caution or warn; admonitory
A story, originally told in folklore, to warn its audience of a certain danger.
In a cautious manner.
(collective) A procession of riders, vehicles, ships, etc.

(historical) A military man serving on horse, (chiefly) early modern cavalry officers who had abandoned the heavy armor of medieval knights. (historical) A gallant: a sprightly young dashing military man.
(military, usually, _, historical, uncountable) The military arm of service that fights while riding horses.
A soldier in the cavalry.
A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside.
A large extinct species of bear, †Ursus spelaeus.
(figurative) To relent; to grant approval against one's initial will.

(uncountable) The activity of applying pigments to the interior surfaces of caves to create images, especially when carried out in prehistoric times. (uncountable) The paintings resulting from this activity regarded collectively, especially if prehistoric; cave art; (countable) an individual painting of this type.
A kind of speleothem, formed as calcite crystallizes on a nucleus such as a grain of sand, in much the same way that a biological pearl forms within a mollusc.
A warning. A qualification or exemption. (law) A notice requesting a postponement of a court proceeding.
An early human or closely related species, popularly held to reside in caves. (informal, figuratively, pejorative) A brutish person, one who behaves in a rough, uncivilized way.
A small (50–100 nanometer) invagination of the plasma membrane in many vertebrate cell types.
A large cave. An underground chamber.
Resembling a cavern in size, shape, or atmosphere.
A part of a horse's bridle that consists of a headstall with a noseband. When a martingale is used, it is attached to the horse's head at the cavesson.
Roe of the sturgeon or of certain other large fish, considered a delicacy.
(intransitive) To criticise for petty or frivolous reasons.
Of or pertaining to a (body) cavity.

(anatomy) A hollow area within the body. A hole or hollow depression in a solid object. (dentistry) A small or large hole in a tooth caused by caries; often also a soft area adjacent to the hole also affected by caries.
(intransitive) To move about carelessly, playfully or boisterously.

The harsh cry of a crow.
To make the harsh cry of a crow, rook, or raven.
Any of several very hot chilli peppers. A powder condiment or spice formed from the dried chilli pepper varieties above.
(formal, intransitive) To stop. (formal, transitive) To stop doing (something).
(legal) To stop and not resume an action.
In warfare, an agreed end to hostilities for a specific purpose. (Typically only temporary).
Without ceasing.
(countable) A coniferous tree of the genus Cedrus in the family Pinaceae. (uncountable) The aromatic wood from a Cedrus tree, or from any of several not closely related trees.
(transitive) To give up; yield to another. [with to]

(orthography) In the spelling of Catalan, French, Portuguese and some other languages, a mark ⟨¸⟩ sometimes placed under the letter c to indicate that it is pronounced /s/ rather than /k/, as in Catalan força, French menaçant, and Portuguese almoço, and also used in various other languages to change the sounds of other letters.
The name of the Latin-script letter C/c.

The upper limit of an object or action. (aviation) The highest altitude at which an aircraft can safely maintain flight. (mathematics) The smallest integer greater than or equal to a given number. (architecture) The overhead interior surface that covers the upper limits of a room.
A fan fixture attached to a ceiling, sometimes with a built-in light.
A pale green colour, possibly tinted with gray. A pale green Chinese glaze. A ceramic ware with a pale green glaze.

A person who officiates at a religious ceremony, especially a marriage or the Eucharist. (Australia, NZ) A person who conducts formal ceremonies in the community, particularly weddings, baby namings, renewals of wedding vows and funerals. A person who is celebrating something.

(transitive) To extol or honour in a solemn manner. (transitive) To honour by rites, by ceremonies of joy and respect, or by refraining from ordinary business; to observe duly. (transitive) To perform or participate in, as a sacrament or solemn rite; to perform with appropriate rites. (transitive, or, intransitive) To engage in joyful activity in appreciation of an event.
famous or widely praised
The formal performance of a solemn rite, such as Christian sacrament. A social gathering for entertainment and fun; a party.

(uncountable, uncommon outside high registers) Fame, renown; the state of being famous or talked-about. [from 17th c.] (countable) A person who has a high degree of recognition by the general population for his or her success or accomplishments; a famous person. [from 19th c.]
A form of celery, Apium graveolens, having an aromatic taproot eaten as a vegetable. [from mid 18th century]
Speed, swiftness.
A European herb (Apium graveolens) of the carrot family. (uncountable, vegetable) The stalks of this herb eaten as a vegetable.
A spice ingredient used in cooking consisting of ground celery seed and salt.
(musical instruments) A musical instrument consisting principally of a set of graduated steel plates struck with hammers that are activated by a keyboard.
of or related to Heaven and the divine. Relating to the sky or outer space, regarded as the realm of the sun, moon, planets, and stars.
(astronomy, astrology) A natural object which is located outside of Earth's atmosphere, such as a comet, an asteroid, the Moon, a planet, the Sun, or a star.
(astronomy) The dynamics of celestial bodies subject to mutual gravitational attraction.
(astronomy) The apparent outer limit of space; an abstract sphere of infinite radius which serves as the imaginary backdrop for celestial objects, and of which the visible sky is one hemisphere.
In a celestial manner; concerning the heavens
(mineral) A mineral with orthorhombic crystals, SrSO4, colourless or white with blue and sometimes red shades.

(US, anatomy) Of, pertaining to or located within the abdomen or abdominal cavity. (US, medicine) Of or pertaining to c(o)eliac disease.
Someone who has celiac disease.
Abstaining from marriage; the state of being unmarried. (by extension) Abstinence from sexual relations.
(chiefly religious) Not married. [from 1827]

(US, NZ, AU, Philippines, informal) A cellular phone. A small room in a monastery or nunnery accommodating one person. [from 14th c.] (obsolete) Specifically, any of the supposed compartments of the brain, formerly thought to be the source of specific mental capacities, knowledge, or memories. [14th–19th c.] A device which stores electrical power; used either singly or together in batteries; the basic unit of a battery. [from 19th c.] (entomology) An area of an insect wing bounded by veins. A room in a prison or jail for one or more inmates. [from 18th c.] (biology, now, chiefly, botany) Any of various chambers in a tissue or organism having specific functions. [from 14th c.] (biology) The basic unit of a living organism, consisting of a quantity of protoplasm surrounded by a cell membrane, which is able to synthesize proteins and replicate itself. [from 19th c.] A small group of people forming part of a larger organization, often an outlawed one. [from 20th c.]
(genetics) A biological tissue or group of individual cells that are genetically identical as a result of dividing mitotically from a single progenitor cell.
(cytology) The semipermeable membrane that surrounds the cytoplasm of a cell.
(biology) The scientific theory that all living organisms are made of cells as the smallest functional unit.

(cytology) A thick, fairly rigid, layer formed around individual cells of bacteria, Archaea, fungi, plants, and algae (but not animals and other protists which generally have cell membranes without cell walls). The cell wall is external to the cell membrane and serves a structural function helping the cell maintain its shape and protecting the cell from damage.

An enclosed underground space, often under a building, used for storage or shelter. A wine collection, especially when stored in a cellar. (slang) Last place in a league or competition; some rank near last place.
A door leading to a cellar.
Someone who plays the cello.
A large unfretted stringed instrument of the violin family with four strings tuned (lowest to highest) C-G-D-A and an endpin to support its weight, usually played with a bow.
(carbohydrate) A disaccharide, found mainly as a repeat unit in cellulose, in which two glucose units are joined with a 1, 4-β linkage
Any of a variety of transparent plastic films, especially one made of processed cellulose.
Of, relating to, consisting of, or resembling a cell or cells.
The dimpled appearance of skin caused by the protrusion of subcutaneous adipose tissue, especially on a woman's hips and thighs.
Any of a variety of thermoplastics created from nitrocellulose and camphor, once used as photographic film.

A complex carbohydrate that forms the main constituent of the cell wall in most plants and is important in the manufacture of numerous products, such as paper, textiles, pharmaceuticals, and explosives.
A cultivar of lettuce harvested primarily for its stem, which measures 15 to 20 centimeters.

(uncountable) The paste-like substance resulting from mixing such a powder with water, or the rock-like substance that forms when it dries. (uncountable) Any material with strong adhesive and cohesive properties such as binding agents, glues, grout.
(transitive) To affix with cement. (figuratively) To make permanent.
A device used in construction in which cement, aggregate and water are slowly mixed together in a revolving drum to form concrete.
(manufacturing) A factory where building cement (for concrete) is manufactured.
(heraldry, rare) Grey, ashen; the blazoning term for grey.
A monk who lives in a religious community, rather than in solitude.
A monument, generally in the form of an empty tomb, erected to honour the dead whose bodies lie elsewhere, especially members of the armed forces who died in battle.

A deep natural well or sinkhole, especially in Mexico and Central America, formed by the collapse of surface limestone that exposes groundwater underneath, and sometimes used by the ancient Mayans for sacrificial offerings.
An ornamental container for burning incense, especially during religious ceremonies.

(Ancient Rome, historical) One of the two magistrates who originally administered the census of citizens, and by Classical times (between the 8th century B.C.E. and the 6th century C.E.) was a high judge of public behaviour and morality. An official responsible for the removal or suppression of objectionable material (for example, if obscene or likely to incite violence) or sensitive content in books, films, correspondence, and other media. (obsolete) One who censures or condemns.
To review for, and if necessary to remove or suppress, content from books, films, correspondence, and other media which is regarded as objectionable (for example, obscene, likely to incite violence, or sensitive).
Relating to a censor.
Addicted to censure and scolding; apt to blame or condemn; severe in making remarks on others, or on their writings or manners.
The use of state or group power to control freedom of expression or press, such as passing laws to prevent undesirable media from being published or propagated.

(computing) Software or hardware used to filter content on the Internet or block Internet access or restrict the running of applications or computer usage, on the basis of content being regarded as objectionable.

The act of blaming, criticizing, or condemning as wrong; reprehension.
(transitive) To criticize harshly. (obsolete, transitive) To form or express a judgment in regard to; to estimate; to judge.
(cellular automata) A count of the number of individual patterns within a larger pattern, most often the ash of a soup or a methuselah.
(money) A subunit of currency equal to one-hundredth of the main unit of currency in many countries. Symbol: ¢.
(Greek mythology) A mythical beast having a horse's body with a man's head and torso in place of the head and neck of the horse.
Centaurea, a genus in the Asteraceae containing species sometimes called centaury

Aged 100 years or more; extremely old. Of or relating to centenarians or a centenary celebration.
One who or that which is at least 100 years old.
(historical, obsolete) Of or relating to hundreds, the administrative unit. Of or related to the number one hundred, particularly [c. 1451]
The hundredth anniversary of an event or happening.

details:
(geometry) The point in the interior of any figure of any number of dimensions that has as its coordinates the arithmetic mean of the coordinates of all points on the perimeter of the figure (or of all points in the interior for a center of volume). A place, especially a building or complex, set aside for some specified function or activity. (engineering) A conical recess or indentation in the end of a shaft or other work, to receive the point of a center, on which the work can turn, as in a lathe. The venue in which the head of government in a centralized state is situated. (AU, NZ) The ring in the gambling game two-up in which the spinner operates. (basketball) The player, generally the tallest, who plays closest to the basket.
(transitive) To cause (an object) to occupy the center of an area. (transitive) To cause (some attribute, such as a mood or voltage) to be adjusted to a value which is midway between the extremes. (intransitive) To concentrate on (something), to pay close attention to (something).
(acting) The area in the center of the stage, especially one towards the front.
(countable) A type of formwork which serves as a temporary structure during the construction of arches and bridges.
(specifically) In the International System of Units and other metric systems of units, multiplying the unit to which it is attached by 10-2. Symbol: c one-hundredth hundred
(metrology) An SI unit of mass equal to 10−2 grams. Symbol: cg
(British spelling) A unit of volume or capacity of one hundredth of a litre. Symbol: cl
(metrology) An SI unit of length equal to 10−2 metres. Symbol: cm
Any arthropod of class Chilopoda, which have a segmented body with one pair of legs per segment and from about 20 to 300 legs in total.
(metrology) An SI unit of time equal to 10−2 seconds. Symbol: cs
Being in the centre. Having or containing the centre of something. Being very important, or key to something.
(geometry) An angle positioned with its vertex at the center of a circle.

(banking) The principal monetary authority of a polity or monetary union; it normally regulates the supply of money, issues currency and controls interest rates. It usually oversees banking activity within its country's borders.
The central area of a city in which there is a concentration of retail and business activities.
The national government of a country such as India and unitary state, in contrast to the lower local government.
Any of various heating systems in which a central source of heat is used to distribute heat (and sometimes hot water) throughout a building in a controlled manner.
(neuroanatomy) In vertebrates, that part of the nervous system comprising the brain, brain stem, and spinal cord.
(computer hardware) The part of a computer that fetches, decodes and executes instructions from memory, possibly through a cache.
(algebra, ring theory) A finite-dimensional associative algebra over some field K that is a simple algebra and whose centre is exactly K.
A system that centralizes, especially an administration of some kind.
The state of being central.
The act or process of centralizing, or the state of being centralized; the act or process of combining or reducing several parts into a whole
To move things physically towards the centre; to consolidate or concentrate To move power to a single, central authority
(location) In a central manner or situation; at, to, through or from the centre.
(soccer) The circle in the centre of the pitch which, at kick-off, the defending team may not enter until the attacking side has touched the ball.
(soccer) A centre-back.
(soccer) midpoint of the halfway line where the ball is placed just before kick-off (tennis) midpoint of the baseline
(British spelling) Something that attracts a lot of attention.
An ornament to be placed in the centre, as of a table, ceiling, etc. A central article or figure.

(physics) In circular motion, the 'reactive' centrifugal force is a real force applied by the accelerating body that is equal and opposite to the centripetal force that is acting on the accelerating body. (erroneous) Centripetal force.

By extension, any device which rotates in order to produce artificial gravity (in the form of centrifugal force)
To rotate something in a centrifuge, typically in order to separate its constituents.
(biology) A barrel-shaped microtubule structure found in most animal cells, important in the process of mitosis (nuclear division).
Directed or moving towards a centre. (neuroanatomy, of a nerve impulse) Directed towards the central nervous system; afferent.
(physics) The force on a rotating or orbiting body in the direction of the centre of rotation.

Of, pertaining to, or advocating centrism.
A person who advocates centrism.

(statistics, cluster analysis, of a cluster of points) the arithmetic mean (alternatively, median) position of a cluster of points in a coordinate system based on some application-dependent measure of distance.
(genetics) The central region of a eukaryotic chromosome where the kinetochore is assembled.
(cytology) An organelle, near the nucleus in the cytoplasm of most organisms, that controls the organization of its microtubules
(historical) An officer of the ancient Roman army, in command of a century of soldiers.

A period of one hundred consecutive years; often specifically a numbered period with conventional start and end dates, e.g., the twentieth century, which stretches from (strictly) 1901 through 2000, or (informally) 1900 through 1999. The first century AD was from 1 to 100. A unit in ancient Roman army, originally of one hundred army soldiers as part of a cohort, later of more varied sizes (but typically containing sixty to seventy or eighty) soldiers or other men (guards, police, firemen), commanded by a centurion.

A Chinese delicacy made by preserving a duck, chicken or quail egg in a mixture of clay, ash, salt, quicklime and rice hulls for several weeks to several months, depending on the method of processing.
An agave (Agave americana) originally from Mexico but cultivated worldwide.
(pathology) headache
Of or relating to the cephalon (the head of a trilobite).
Any mollusc of the class Cephalopoda, which includes squid, cuttlefish, octopus, nautiloids etc.
Any of a class of natural and synthetic antibiotics developed from Acremonium fungi, having a cepham structure.
Of or relating to cepstra or their analysis.
(signal processing) The inverse Fourier transform of the logarithm of a magnitude spectrum; used especially in voice analysis.

Made of material produced by the high-temperature firing of inorganic, nonmetallic rocks and minerals.
(uncountable) A hard, brittle, inorganic, nonmetallic material, usually made from a material, such as clay, then firing it at a high temperature.
The art or science of making ceramic objects. Ceramic objects as a group.
(biochemistry) Any of various lipids formed by linking a fatty acid to sphingosine and found widely but in small amounts in plant and animal tissue
(zoology) Any of many dinosaurs of the infraorder Ceratosauria.
(countable) A type of grass (such as wheat, rice or oats) cultivated for its edible grains. (uncountable) The grains of such a grass.
A snack composed of some form of breakfast cereal that has been compressed into a bar shape and is held together with some form of edible adhesive.
(anatomy, relational) Of or pertaining to the cerebellum.

(neuroanatomy) Part of the hindbrain in vertebrates. In humans it lies between the brainstem and the back of the cerebrum and is formed of two lateral lobes and a median lobe. It plays an important role in sensory perception, motor output, balance and posture.
(anatomy, relational) Of or relating to the brain, cerebrum, or cerebral cortex. Intellectual rather than emotional or physical.
(neuroanatomy) The grey, folded, outermost layer of the cerebrum that is responsible for higher brain processes such as sensation, voluntary muscle movement, thought, reasoning, and memory.
(neuroanatomy) One of the two regions of the brain that are delineated by the body's median plane.
(neurology, pathology) A group of non-progressive, non-contagious conditions, caused by brain damage before birth or during infancy, characterized by impairment of muscular coordination.
(anatomy) Of or pertaining to brain or spine (particularly the spinal cord).
(neuroanatomy) A bodily fluid filling the third ventricle and surrounding the interthalamic adhesion.
(anatomy) Relating to the blood vessels that run to or from the brain.
(medicine, formal, sometimes, euphemistic) Stroke (loss of brain function arising when the blood supply to the brain is suddenly interrupted).

(neuroanatomy) The principal and most anterior part of the brain in vertebrates, which is located in the front area of the skull and divided into two hemispheres, left and right, separated by a fissure. In humans it is the largest part of the brain and is responsible for the integration of complex sensory functions and the initiation and coordination of voluntary activity, and the higher mental functions such as consciousness, thought, reason, emotion, and memory.
Of, relating to, consisting of, or used in a ceremony.
According to the required or usual ceremonies, formalities, or rituals; specifically (Christianity, obsolete) , to ceremonial laws in the Bible.

A ritual, with religious or cultural significance. An official gathering to celebrate, commemorate, or otherwise mark some event. (uncountable) A formal socially established behaviour, often in relation to people of different ranks; formality.
Any of the genus Cereus, either as currently or formerly defined, of plants of the cactus family, natives to the Americas, from California to Chile.

(of textiles, especially silk) Cherry-colored; a light bright red.
A deep, bright red colour tinted with pink.
A chemical element (symbol Ce) with an atomic number of 58, a very soft, ductile, silvery-white metal that tarnishes when exposed to air.

Sure in one's mind, positive; absolutely confident in the truth of something. Not to be doubted or denied; established as a fact. Sure to happen, inevitable; assured. (euphemism, preceded by "a") Used to denote that the speaker is referring to a specific person or thing that they do not want to name directly, implying that the listener should infer the identity of the referent.
Having been determined but not specified.
In a way which is certain; with certainty. Without doubt, surely. An emphatic affirmative answer; of course.
The state of being certain.
(of a document) That can or must be certified.
A document containing a certified statement.
The act of certifying.
(transitive) To attest to (a fact) as the truth.
(uncountable) Sureness, certainty.

Sky-blue.
(countable, and, uncountable) A greenish-blue color.
(mineral) A mineral form of lead carbonate, PbCO3, that is an ore of lead.
(anatomy, relational) Of or pertaining to the neck. (anatomy, relational) Of or pertaining to the cervix.

(pathology, oncology) A type of cancer of the cervix of the uterus which can afflict some female mammals including humans. The term usually does not refer to cancer of the neck or other parts of the anatomy which use the term cervix.
A small latex or silicone contraceptive device that fits over the cervix and stays in place either by suction or by surface viscosity.
(anatomy) Any of the seven vertebrae of the neck.
(pathology) Inflammation of the cervix.
Of or relating to the neck or cervical vertebrae.
(anatomy) Relating to the cervix and thorax.
(biology) Pertaining to the cervix and vagina.
(zoology) Any animal of the family Cervidae; a deer.
(now, specifically) The cervix uteri, or lower, narrow portion of the uterus where it joins with the top end of the vagina.
(formal) A ceasing or discontinuance, for example of an action, whether temporary or final.
An underground pit where sewage is held. (by extension) A filthy place.
An animal belonging to the infraorder Cetacea, including dolphins, porpoises, and whales.
(organic compound) The aliphatic hydrocarbon C16H34 (hexadecane) used as a standard for diesel fuel.
(carboxylic acid, pharmaceutical drug) A major metabolite of hydroxyzine, an antihistamine used in the treatment of allergies, hay fever, angioedema, and urticaria.
The branch of zoology concerned with the infraorder Cetacea, which includes whales, dolphins, and porpoises.
(cooking) Raw seafood cured by marination in an acidic medium such as citrus, vinegar, or other souring agent, found primarily in Latin America.
Compare; compare to; compare with.
(dance) A ballroom dance to a Latin American rhythm. (music genre) The music for this dance.
(mineral) A black triclinic mineral composed of thallium, lead, antimony, arsenic and sulfur Tl4Pb2(Sb,As)20S34.
Any of several cracid birds, of the genus Ortalis, limited to the Americas, that resemble the guans.
A loose robe made from a single cloth, worn as a combination head covering, veil and shawl by chiefly Muslim women (and occasionally by those of other faiths) in Iran and South Asia.
(business) A large, family-controlled, South Korean business conglomerate.

details:
Heat excited by friction. Injury or wear caused by friction. (archaic, countable, uncountable) Vexation; irritation of mind; rage.
(transitive, figurative) To excite passion or anger in; to fret; to irritate. (intransitive) To rub; to come together so as to wear by rubbing; to wear by friction. (intransitive, figurative) To have a feeling of vexation; to be vexed; to fret; to be irritated.
The inedible parts of a grain-producing plant. Straw or hay cut up fine for the food of cattle. (figurative) Any excess or unwanted material, resource, or person; anything worthless.
A small passerine bird, Fringilla coelebs, of the finch family, found throughout Europe and eastward to Iran and eastern Mediterranean coastlands.
The act by which something is chafed.

Distress of mind caused by a failure of aims or plans, want of appreciation, mistakes etc; vexation or mortification.
(transitive) To bother or vex; to mortify.

A series of interconnected rings or links usually made of metal. A series of stores or businesses with the same brand name. (computing theory, of a problem) That is in a given complexity class and is such that every other problem in the class can be reduced to it (usually in polynomial time or logarithmic space).
(ambitransitive) To finish; to make done; to reach the end. (transitive) To make whole or entire.
Finished.
In a complete manner; thoroughly. To the fullest extent or degree; totally.
The state or condition of being complete.

Not simple, easy, or straightforward; complicated. (mathematics, of a number) Having the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i is (by definition) the imaginary square root of −1. (mathematics, analysis, of a function) Whose range is a subset of the complex numbers. (mathematics, algebra) Whose coefficients are complex numbers; defined over the field of complex numbers.
A collection of buildings with a common purpose, such as a university or military base. An assemblage of related things; a collection. (psychology) A group of emotionally charged ideas or mental factors, unconsciously associated by the individual with a particular subject, arising from repressed instincts, fears, or desires and often resulting in mental abnormality. (chemistry) A structure consisting of a central atom or molecule weakly connected to surrounding atoms or molecules, as for example coordination complexes in inorganic chemistry and protein complexes in biochemistry.
(chemistry, intransitive) To form a complex with another substance.
(mathematics) The branch of mathematics that studies holomorphic functions.
(mathematics) Of a complex number x, the complex number \overline x formed by changing the sign of the imaginary part: The complex conjugate of a + bi is a - bi.
(mathematics) A function whose range is a subset of the set of complex numbers.
(complex analysis) A number of the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i denotes the imaginary unit.
The quality, colour, or appearance of the skin on the face.
(uncountable) The state of being complex; intricacy; entanglement. (countable) That which is and renders complex; intricacy; complication.

An act of complying. (medicine) The accuracy with which a patient follows an agreed treatment plan (uncountable) The state of being compliant. (mechanics) A measure of the extension or displacement of a loaded structure; its flexibility (uncountable, business) The department of a business that ensures all government regulations are complied with.
Willing to comply; submissive; willing to do what someone wants. Compatible with or following guidelines, specifications, rules, or laws.
(transitive) To make complex; to modify so as to make something intricate or difficult.
Difficult or convoluted.

The state of being complicated; intricate or confused relation of parts; complexity. (medicine) A disease or diseases, or adventitious circumstances or conditions, coexistent with and modifying a primary disease, but not necessarily connected with it.
Associated with or participating in an activity, especially one of a questionable nature.
The state of being complicit; involvement as a partner or accomplice, especially in a crime or other wrongdoing.

An expression of praise, congratulation, or respect. (uncountable) Complimentary language; courtesy, flattery.
(ambitransitive) To pay a compliment (to someone); to express a favourable opinion (of someone).
In the nature of a compliment.
(Christianity) The last of the canonical hours, sung just before retiring to bed.
To yield assent; to accord; to acquiesce, agree, consent; to adapt oneself, to conform.
A smaller, self-contained part of a larger entity. Often refers to a manufactured object that is part of a larger device.
(intransitive) To be in agreement (with); to be of an accord. [from 16th c.] (reflexive) To behave (in a given manner). [from 17th c.]

(transitive) To make something by merging parts. [from later 15th c.] (transitive, or, intransitive) To construct by mental labor; to think up; particularly, to produce or create a literary or musical work. (transitive) To make up the whole; to constitute. To settle (an argument, dispute etc.); to come to a settlement.
Showing composure.
Especially, one who composes music.

Made up of multiple components; compound or complex.
A mixture of different components.
(mathematics) A function of one or more independent variables, at least one of which is itself a function of one or more other independent variables; a function of function(s).
The general makeup of a thing or person. [from 14th c.] A work of music, literature or art. [from 17th c.] (painting, photography) The arrangement and flow of elements in a picture.

The decayed remains of organic matter that has rotted into a natural fertilizer.
To produce compost, let organic matter decay into fertilizer.
(gardening) a pile of garden or other organic waste which is left to decompose. See also compost.
Suitable for compost.
Calmness of mind or temperament.
A dessert made of fruit cooked in sugary syrup.

Composed of elements; not simple.
Anything made by combining several things. (chemistry) A substance formed by chemical bonding of two or more elements in definite proportions by weight.
A group of buildings situated close together, e.g. for a school or block of offices.
(intransitive, finance) To increase in value with interest, where the interest is earned on both the principal sum and prior earned interest. (horse racing, intransitive) Of a horse: to fail to maintain speed.
(weapons) A modern bow that uses pulleys and cables to help with the drawing and releasing of the bowstring.
(zootomy) A visual organ found in arthropods such as insects and crustaceans. It consists of one to thousands of tiny independent photoreception units.
(banking, finance) Interest, as on a loan or a bank account, that is calculated on the total on the principal plus accumulated unpaid interest.
(grammar) A sentence that has two or more independent clauses, joined by a conjunction (such as 'but', 'and') and/or punctuation (such as ',').
(linguistics) A word composed of two or more stems.
(Marxism) A section of an indigenous middle class allied with foreign investors, multinational corporations, bankers, and military interests.
(transitive) To understand or grasp fully and thoroughly; to plumb. [from 14th c.] (now, _, rare) To include, comprise; to contain. [from 14th c.]
One who comprehends.
The characteristic of being comprehensible; clarity.
Able to be comprehended.
A thorough understanding.
Broadly or completely covering; including a large proportion of something.

(medicine) A multiply folded piece of cloth, a pouch of ice, etc., used to apply to a patient's skin, cover the dressing of wounds, and placed with the aid of a bandage to apply pressure on an injury.
(transitive) To make smaller; to press or squeeze together, or to make something occupy a smaller space or volume. (intransitive) To be pressed together or folded by compression into a more economic, easier format. (transitive) To condense into a more economic, easier format. (computing, transitive) To make digital information smaller by encoding it using fewer bits.
Air which has been reduced in volume and increased in pressure for use in industrial processes or for cleaning.
The degree to which something is compressible.

An increase in density; the act of compressing, or the state of being compressed; compaction. (automotive) The cycle of an internal combustion engine during which the fuel and air mixture is compressed. (computing) The process by which data is compressed.
(clothing) An elasticated sock worn to help prevent the occurrence of venous disorders such as edema, phlebitis, and thrombosis.
A device that produces pressure, such as a gas compressor that produces pressurized gas. (computing) A program or algorithm for compressing data.

(transitive) To be made up of; to consist of (especially a comprehensive list of parts). [from the earlier 15th c.] (sometimes, proscribed, usually in the passive) To compose; to constitute. [from the 17th c.]

The settlement of differences by arbitration or by consent reached by mutual concessions.
(ambitransitive) To bind by mutual agreement. To adjust and settle by mutual concessions; to compound. To pledge by some act or declaration; to endanger the life, reputation, etc., of, by some act which can not be recalled; to expose to suspicion. (transitive) To breach (a security system).
That compromises somebody or something; incriminating.

An irrational need or irresistible urge to perform some action, often despite negative consequences. The use of authority, influence, or other power to force (compel) a person or persons to act. The lawful use of violence (i.e. by the administration).
Uncontrolled or reactive and irresistible.
In a compulsive manner; obsessively.
In a compulsory manner.
Required; obligatory; mandatory.
(legal, Australia, New Zealand) The power of a state to expropriate private land within its jurisdiction for public use.
(legal, education) A period of time in a child's life during which the child must receive schooling as required by law.
(legal, UK, Ireland) The power of a state to expropriate private land within its jurisdiction for public use.
A pricking of conscience or a feeling of regret, especially one which is slight or fleeting.
The act or process of computing; calculation; reckoning.
Of or relating to computation.

(linguistics, computer science) An interdisciplinary field dealing with the statistical and/or rule-based modeling of natural language from a computational perspective. This modeling is not limited to any particular field of linguistics.
(transitive) To reckon, calculate.

A form of radiography which uses computer software to create images, or slices, at various planes of depth from images taken around a body or volume of interest. Sometimes called “computerized tomography”. (The radiation used is X-rays unless otherwise specified.)

(now, rare, chiefly, historical) A person employed to perform computations; one who computes. [from 17th c.] A programmable electronic device that performs mathematical calculations and logical operations, especially one that can process, store and retrieve large amounts of data very quickly; now especially, a small one for personal or home use employed for manipulating text or graphics, accessing the Internet, or playing games or media. [from 20th c.]
An electronic game, especially a game played using a general-purpose computer (as opposed to a game console).

(computing) The ability to operate a personal computer, including its associated hardware and software (but not necessarily to understand the underlying electronics or a programming language). [from late 20th c.]
A complete piece of software.
The study of computers and their architecture, languages, and applications, in all aspects, as well as the mathematical structures that relate to computers and computation.
One who studies or practises computer science.
A branch of computer science that addresses enforcement of 'secure' behavior on the operation of computers.

(computing) A program which can covertly transmit itself between computers via networks (especially the Internet) or removable storage such as disks and USB drives, often causing damage to systems and data.

(artificial intelligence) The science and technology of machines that see, concerned with the theory for building artificial systems that obtain information from images, such as a video sequence, views from multiple cameras, or multi-dimensional data from a medical scanner.
The act of computerizing something, or something computerized.
(transitive, computing) To equip with a computer or a computer system.
The use of a computer or computers. The study of computers and computer programming.

A mate, companion, or associate. [from 1590s] A companion in battle; fellow soldier. (communism, by extension) A fellow socialist, communist or other similarly politically aligned person. [from 1884] (communism) A non-hierarchical title, functionally similar to "Mr.", "Mrs.", "Miss", "Ms." etc, in a communist, socialist, or rarely in an Islamist state. [from 1884]

A disadvantage of something, especially when contrasted with its advantages (pros).
(transitive, informal) To trick, lie or defraud, usually for personal gain.
A person who uses confidence tricks to defraud or swindle people after first gaining their trust with a series of confidence games; a scam operator, confidence trickster.
A swindle in which the mark, or victim, is defrauded after his or her trust has been won.
Of or pertaining to a striving action.
To join or link together, as though in a chain.
(countable) A series of links united; a series or order of things depending on each other, as if linked together; a chain, a succession.
Curved like the inner surface of a sphere or bowl.
(uncountable) The state of being concave (countable) A concave structure or surface
(transitive) To hide something from view or from public knowledge, to try to keep something secret.
(countable) Something that, or someone who, conceals. (countable, uncountable) A cosmetic designed to cover blemishes.
The practice of keeping secrets.
To yield or suffer; to surrender; to grant To grant, as a right or privilege; to make concession of.

(countable, rhetoric, literature) An ingenious expression or metaphorical idea, especially in extended form or used as a literary or rhetorical device. [from 16th c.] (uncountable) Overly high self-esteem; vain pride; hubris. [from 17th c.]
Having an excessively favourable opinion of one's abilities, appearance, etc.; egotistical and vain.
Capable of being conceived or imagined.
(ambitransitive) To have a child; to become pregnant (with). (transitive) To develop; to form in the mind; to imagine. (transitive) To understand (someone).

A substance that is in a condensed form.
(ergative) To bring to, or direct toward, a common center; to unite more closely; to gather into one body, mass, or force. To increase the strength and diminish the bulk of, as of a liquid or an ore; to intensify, by getting rid of useless material; to condense. To approach or meet in a common center; to consolidate. (intransitive) To focus one's thought or attention (on).

The act, process or ability of concentrating; the process of becoming concentrated, or the state of being concentrated. The act or process of removing the dress of ore and of reducing the valuable part to smaller compass, as by currents of air or water. The proportion of a substance in a whole. (physical chemistry) The amount of solute in a solution measured in suitable units (e.g., parts per million (ppm))

A camp where large numbers of people, especially political prisoners, prisoners of war, refugees etc., are detained for the purpose of confining them in one place, typically with inadequate or inhumane facilities. [from 19th c.]

(geometry) Having a common center. (physiology) (of a motion) in the direction of contraction of a muscle. (E.g. extension of the lower arm via the elbow joint while contracting the triceps and other elbow extensor muscles; closing of the jaw while flexing the masseter).

Understanding retained in the mind, from experience, reasoning and imagination; a generalization (generic, basic form), or abstraction (mental impression), of a particular set of instances or occurrences (specific, though different, recorded manifestations of the concept).
An album of music where the content follows an overall theme or narrative.

A diagram showing the relationships among concepts, with the concepts drawn in boxes that are connected with labelled arrows denoting the relationships between concepts, such as "is a", "gives rise to", "results in", "is required by," or "contributes to".
The power or faculty of apprehending of forming an idea in the mind; the power of recalling a past sensation or perception; the ability to form mental abstractions.
Of, or relating to concepts or mental conception.
A genre of art in which the transmission of ideas is more important than the creation of an art object
To interpret a phenomenon by forming a concept.
In a conceptual manner.

That which affects one’s welfare or happiness. A matter of interest to someone. The expression of solicitude, anxiety, or compassion toward a thing or person. A business, firm or enterprise; a company.
(transitive) To relate or belong to; to have reference to or connection with; to affect the interest of; to be of importance to.
Showing concern.

Causing concern; worrying.
Regarding, respecting.

(uncountable) An agreement in a design or plan; a union formed by mutual communication of opinions and views; an accordance in a scheme; harmony; a simultaneous action. (uncountable) Musical accordance or harmony; concord. (countable) A musical performance, usually public, in which several performers or instruments take part.
(transitive) To plan; to devise; to arrange.
A large building where concerts are performed.
A musical instrument, like the various accordions, that is a member of the free-reed family of musical instruments, typically having buttons on both ends.
(music, US) The first violin in a symphony orchestra, which normally plays violin solos.
(music) A piece of music for one or more solo instruments and orchestra.

(by extension) Any admission of the validity or rightness of a point; an instance of this. (Canadian) A concession road: a narrow road between tracts of farmland, especially in Ontario, from their origin during the granting of concessions (see above). A right to use land or an offshore area for a specific purpose, such as oil exploration.

The degree by which a loan or trade reduces the lender's or one trading partner's returns in comparison with what they would get at full market rates. A mechanism by which a loan or trade agreement results in the lender or one party receiving less than full market value.
Of, pertaining to, or being a concession; conceding.
The shell of this sea animal. A musical instrument made from a large spiral seashell, somewhat like a trumpet. Synonym of concher (“machine used to refine the flavour and texture of chocolate”).
A process in the manufacture of chocolate in which the flavour and texture is refined by warming and grinding, either in a traditional concher or between rollers.
The study of molluscs and their shells.
One who attends to the wishes of hotel guests. (British) One who attends to the maintenance of a building and provides services to its tenants and visitors.
(transitive) To make calm and content, or regain the goodwill of; to placate; to propitiate.

(legal) A form of alternative dispute resolution, similar to but less formal than mediation, in which the parties bring their dispute to a neutral third party, who helps lower tensions, improve communications and explore possible solutions.
Brief, yet including all important information.
In a concise manner, briefly, without excessive length.
The property of being concise; succinctness.

A closed assembly at which cardinals elect a pope. A group of cardinals assembled to elect a new pope. (by extension) A closed, private, or secret meeting, especially one of an ecclesiastical nature. The set of apartments in which cardinals are secluded while the process to elect a pope takes place.
(intransitive) To end; to come to an end. (transitive) To come to a conclusion, to a final decision. (obsolete) To include; to comprehend; to shut up together; to embrace; to confine.

The end, finish, close or last part of something. The outcome or result of a process or act. A decision reached after careful thought. (logic) In an argument or syllogism, the proposition that follows as a necessary consequence of the premises. arrangement; settlement.
Pertaining to a conclusion. Providing an end to something; decisive.
In a conclusive manner; with finality.
To prepare something by mixing various ingredients, especially to prepare food for cooking.
A mixture prepared in such a way.
Accompanying; conjoining; attending; concurrent. [from early 17th c.]
A state of agreement; harmony; union.
(chiefly, _, Bible) An alphabetical verbal index showing the places in the text of a book where each principal word may be found, with its immediate context in each place.
Agreeing or harmonious; consistent (with).
A formal agreement between two parties, especially between a church and a state; specifically, an agreement between the Pope and a government.

A large open space in or in front of a building where people can gather, particularly one joining various paths, as in a rail station or airport terminal, or providing access to and linking the platforms in a railway terminus.

definition:

  2. concreto
  3. de concreto | 1. concreto | 1. hormigonar
  2. concretizar
details:
Real, actual, tangible. Particular, specific, rather than general. Being or applying to actual things, rather than abstract qualities or categories. (obsolete) Not liquid or fluid; solid. (not comparable) Made of concrete (building material).
(countable, uncountable) A building material created by mixing cement, water, and aggregate such as gravel and sand.
(usually, transitive) To cover with or encase in concrete (building material). (usually, transitive) To solidify: to change from being abstract to being concrete (actual, real).
(grammar) A noun that denotes something tangible or material, such as a person or place.
(linguistics) A term which expresses material facts, actions and events in physical reality relating to possible causes and means.
In a concrete manner, physically, definitely
The process of aggregating or coalescing into a mass.
(art) An abstractionist painting movement that evolved in the 1930s.
(transitive) To make concrete, substantial, real, or tangible; to represent or embody a concept through a particular instance or example.
The state of cohabiting or living together as man and woman while not married.
A woman who lives with a man, but who is not a wife.
An ardent desire, especially sexual desire; lust.
Amorous; lustful.

To agree (in action or opinion); to have a common opinion; to coincide; to correspond. To meet in the same point; to combine or conjoin; to contribute or help towards a common object or effect. (obsolete) To run together; to meet.
Agreement; concurring.
Happening at the same time; simultaneous. Belonging to the same period; contemporary.
In a concurrent manner; at the same time.

(obsolete, seismology) A violent collision or shock. (uncountable, _, in, _, Commonwealth, countable, _) An injury to part of the body, most especially the brain, caused by a violent blow, followed by loss of function.

(transitive) To strongly criticise or denounce; to excoriate. (transitive) To judicially announce a verdict upon a finding of guilt; To sentence (transitive) To confer eternal divine punishment upon. (transitive) To adjudge (a building) as being unfit for habitation.
The act of condemning or pronouncing to be wrong. The act of judicially condemning, or adjudging guilty, unfit for use, or forfeited; the act of dooming to punishment or forfeiture.
(physics) A liquid that is the product of condensation of a gas, i.e. of steam.
The act or process of condensing or of being condensed (physics, physical chemistry) The conversion of a gas to a liquid.

(transitive) To concentrate toward the essence by making more close, compact, or dense, thereby decreasing size or volume. (transitive, chemistry) To transform from a gaseous state into a liquid state via condensation. (intransitive, chemistry) To be transformed from a gaseous state into a liquid state.
Milk that has been reduced and sweetened to the consistency of syrup.

To come down from a superior position and do something; to deign; (with a negative connotation) to stoop. To treat someone as though inferior; to talk down to someone; to patronize. (nonstandard, rare) To treat (someone) as though inferior; to talk down to (someone); to patronize.
Assuming a tone of superiority, or a patronizing attitude.
Something used to enhance the flavor of food, for example, salt or pepper, especially when added by the eater to taste rather than by the cook.

A particular state of being. A requirement. A logical clause or phrase that a conditional statement uses. The phrase can either be true or false. (law) A clause in a contract or agreement indicating that a certain contingency may modify the principal obligation in some way. The health status of a medical patient.
To subject to the process of acclimation.
(legal) a condition depending upon an uncertain event which must be fulfilled before an obligation arises or a legal transaction takes effect.
(legal) A condition depending upon an uncertain event which, if fulfilled, brings an end to an obligation or legal transaction.

Limited by a condition. (logic) Stating that one sentence is true if another is true.
(grammar) The conditional mood.
(grammar) A combination of the conditional mood and the perfect tense, roughly corresponding to English 'I would have...'
(uncountable) A state of being subject to conditions.
under specified conditions
A response, to a stimulus, that has been acquired by operant conditioning.
Anything that improves the condition of something.
The process of modifying a person or animal's behaviour. Any preparation or training, especially athletic training of the body.
(countable, usually, in the plural) An expression of comfort, support, or sympathy offered to the family and friends of somebody who has died.

Expressing sympathy to someone, especially after learning of a close death.
comfort, support, or sympathy offered especially to the family and friends of somebody who has died.

A flexible sleeve made of latex or other impermeable material such as polyurethane or sheepskin, worn over an erect penis during sexual intercourse as a contraceptive or as a way to prevent the spread of STIs during PIV, anal, or oral. (broadly) Any of various forms of flexible sleeve or barrier, variously shaped for either penetrative or receptive body parts, made of latex or other impermeable material such as polyurethane or sheepskin, worn (by anyone with ) during sexual activity to prevent pregnancy or the spread of STIs.

(US, Canada, Philippines) A building or complex of buildings that provides multiple residential units each of which is owned separately but whose grounds, structure, etc. (if any) are owned jointly. [from 20th c.] (US, Canada, Philippines) The system of ownership by which such condominiums operate.

(transitive) To forgive, excuse or overlook (something that is considered morally wrong, offensive, or generally disliked). (transitive, legal) To forgive (marital infidelity or other marital offense). (transitive) To allow, accept or permit (something that is considered morally wrong, offensive, or generally disliked).

Either of two New World vultures, Vultur gryphus of the Andes or Gymnogyps californianus, a nearly extinct vulture of the mountains of California. (golf) The completion of a hole four strokes under par (a quadruple birdie, triple eagle, or double albatross).
Tending to contribute to, encourage, or bring about some result.

definition:

details:
The act or method of controlling or directing.
(archaic, transitive) To lead, or guide; to escort. (transitive) To lead; to direct; to be in charge of (people or tasks) (transitive, reflexive) To behave. (transitive) To serve as a medium for conveying; to transmit (heat, light, electricity, etc.) (intransitive) To act as a conductor (as of heat, electricity, etc.); to carry.
(physics) The conveying of heat or electricity through material.
Able to conduct electrical current or heat.
The ability of a material to conduct electricity, heat, fluid or sound (physics) The reciprocal of resistivity

(musician) A person who conducts an orchestra, choir or other music ensemble; a professional whose occupation is conducting. (rail transport) A person who takes tickets on public transportation and also helps passengers. (physics) Something that can transmit electricity, heat, light, or sound.
A pipe or channel for conveying water, etc.
Relating to or resembling a condyle.
(anatomy) A smooth prominence on a bone where it forms a joint with another bone.

(geometry) A surface of revolution formed by rotating a segment of a line around another line that intersects the first line. (geometry) A solid of revolution formed by rotating a triangle around one of its altitudes. (anatomy) Any of the small cone-shaped structures in the retina. (topology) A space formed by taking the direct product of a given space with a closed interval and identifying all of one end to a point. The fruit of a conifer.
(Wicca) Mental energy amassed individually or collectively for a magickal purpose, visualized as a cone whose base encompasses the circumference of the magic circle of practitioners.
(ambitransitive, psychology) To fabricate memories in order to fill gaps in one's memory.
A food item prepared very sweet, frequently decorated in fine detail, and often preserved with sugar, such as a candy, sweetmeat, fruit preserve, pastry, or cake.
A candy, sweetmeat; a confection. (obsolete) One who makes confections; a confectioner.
A manufacturer of or dealer in confections (sweets, candies, sweet pastries, and other sweet food items).
Cream used by confectioners to make pies, etc.

(uncountable) Foodstuffs that taste very sweet, taken as a group; candies, sweetmeats and confections collectively. (uncountable) The business or occupation of manufacturing confectionery; the skill or work of a confectioner.
An alliance.
Of, pertaining to, or being a confederation.
Of, relating to, or united in a confederacy
A union or alliance of states or political organizations.
The advocacy of confederation as a means of government.
(transitive) To grant as a possession; to bestow. [from 16th c.] (intransitive) To talk together, to consult, discuss; to collogue. [from 16th c.]

(business) An event organized by a for-profit or non-profit organization to discuss a pressing issue, such as a new product, market trend or government regulation, with a range of speakers. (Philippines, sports) A constituent tournament of a sports league in a given season.
(intransitive, transitive) To admit to the truth, particularly in the context of sins or crimes committed.

The open admittance of having done something (especially something bad). A formula in which the articles of faith are comprised; a creed to be assented to or signed, as a preliminary to admission to membership of a church; a confession of faith.
(Roman Catholicism) A small room where confession—the Sacrament of Penance—is performed in private with a priest.
The degree or quality of being confessional.
(Eastern Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism) A priest who hears confession and then gives absolution.
Small pieces or strips (streamers) of colored paper or other material (metal, plaster, etc) generally thrown about at festive occasions, especially at weddings and in victory celebrations.
A person in whom one can confide or share one's secrets: a friend.
(intransitive, with in) To take (someone) into one's confidence, to speak in secret with.
Self-assurance. A feeling of certainty; firm trust or belief; faith. Information held in secret; a piece of information shared but to thence be kept in secret.
(statistics) A range defined such that there is a fixed probability that the value of the measured parameter will fall within the range.
Very sure of something; positive.
Kept, or meant to be kept, secret within a certain circle of persons; not intended to be known publicly
(uncountable) The property of being confidential.
In a confidential manner.
In a confident manner; with confidence; with strong assurance; positively.
Capable of being configured; customisable; permitting rearrangement or adjustment.
The form of a thing, as depending on the relative placement of the parts of a thing's shape.
(transitive) To set up or arrange something in such a way that it is ready for operation for a particular purpose, or to someone's particular liking

(mostly, in the plural) A boundary or limit.
(transitive) To restrict (someone or something) to a particular scope or area; to keep in or within certain bounds. [from 17th c.]
An enclosed area with limited space and accessibility.
The act of confining or the state of being confined.
To strengthen; to make firm or resolute. (transitive, Christianity) To administer the sacrament of confirmation on (someone). To assure the accuracy of previous statements.
(religion) A candidate for confirmation or affirmation of baptism.

An official indicator that things will happen as planned. A verification that something is true or has happened. A ceremony of sealing and conscious acknowledgement of the faith in many Christian churches, typically around the ages of 14 to 18; considered a sacrament in some churches, including Catholicism, but not in most Protestant churches.

(psychology) A cognitive bias towards confirmation of the hypothesis under study; a psychological tendency to look for and accept information which supports one's values and worldview and reject that which conflicts with it.
(formal) Having a settled habit; inveterate or habitual. (Christianity) Having received the rite of confirmation.
Any man uninterested in committed relationships.
(transitive) To use one's authority to lay claim to and separate a possession from its holder.
The act or process of confiscating.
a preserve or jelly/jam of candied fruit
A large fire extending to many objects, or over a large space; a general burning.

(by extension) To fail to properly distinguish or keep separate (things); to mistakenly treat (them) as equivalent. (by extension) To deliberately draw a false equivalence or association, typically in a tacit or implicit manner as propaganda and/or an intentional distortion or misrepresentation of the subject matter.

An ornate tent. A structure, sometimes temporary, erected to house exhibits at a fair, etc. A light roofed structure used as a shelter in a public place.
One of many flat stones used to pave an outdoor area.

(military, history) Most usually, a very large shield fitted with a stand, like a small moveable wall, carried in front to protect all or most of the bearer's body that could be positioned independently of the user, such as a crossbowman, often with a projecting ridge running vertically down the center. However, smaller, more standard shield types were also termed as such, with the central verticle ridge as a defining feature.
The soft foot of a mammal or other animal, generally a quadruped, that has claws or nails; comparable to a human hand or foot.
(New Zealand) An edible univalve mollusc of the genus Haliotis, having a shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

A pivoted catch designed to fall into a notch on a ratchet wheel so as to allow movement in only one direction (e.g. on a windlass or in a clock mechanism), or alternatively to move the wheel in one direction. A similar device to prevent motion in other mechanisms besides ratchets.

details:
(chess) The most numerous chess piece, or a similar piece in a similar game. In chess, each side starts with eight; moves are only forward, and attacks are only diagonally or en passant. (idiomatic) A person being manipulated by another, being used to some end. An instance of pawning something. (rare) A pawnshop; pawnbroker.
(transitive) To give as security on a loan of money; especially, to deposit (something) at a pawn shop.
A person who makes monetary loans at interest, taking personal property as security – which may be sold if not redeemed.
The business premises of a pawnbroker; where loans are made, with personal property as security
Asimina, a genus of trees and shrubs native to eastern North America, especially common pawpaw (Asimina triloba). Any of several types of trees having edible fruit: The fruit of these trees.

Money given in return for work; salary or wages.
(ambitransitive) To give money or other compensation to in exchange for goods or services. (nautical, transitive) To cover (the bottom of a vessel, a seam, a spar, etc.) with tar or pitch, or a waterproof composition of tallow, resin, etc.; to smear. (transitive) To be profitable for.
(idiomatic, intransitive) To attend; to be attentive; to focus one's attention.
(figuratively) To avenge, to exact revenge.
The difference in salaries between one group and another.
A level indicating a base salary (in the US applying to military and government employees).

details: (transitive, informal) To bribe, especially to deter oversight. (intransitive) To become worthwhile; to produce a net benefit. (transitive) To pay back; to repay. (transitive) To pay back (repay) the entirety of a loan, thereby effecting the release of a lien on (the thing that was financed).
To demonstrate or profess respect to (someone or an ideal); to behave in a manner that demonstrates respect to (someone or an ideal).
(UK, Ireland, Australia, rest of Commonwealth, sometimes, Canada) An increase in salary or wages.
(idiomatic, of a job) To provide enough income to sustain one's lifestyle.
(idiomatic) To incur the negative consequences of (one’s own or someone else’s) actions or decisions.

(British) A payment method where the charge of a service is taken automatically, usually in small amounts, after the usage, in contrast of paying before usage. Used especially of mobile phones and transport ticketing.
A payment in full; the state of having been paid in full. A return on investment. A reward. (informal) A bribe.
(uncountable) An act of revenge. (countable) A benefit, reward, a form of recompense.
(US) Money received on payday as payment for work performed.
The day of the week or month, or the specific day, on which an employee's wages or salary is paid.
one to whom money is paid.
One who pays; specifically, the person by whom a bill or note has been, or should be, paid.
That part of a cargo that produces revenue.
(uncountable) The act of paying. (countable) An instance of that act; a sum of money paid in exchange#Noun for goods or services, or the transaction#Noun that conveys it.

(finance, chiefly, banking) An instruction from a sender to a receiving bank, transmitted orally, electronically, or in writing, to pay, or to cause another bank to pay a fixed and determinable amount of money to a beneficiary.
An amount of money paid out.
A public telephone that requires prepayment to operate, generally via the insertion of coins or a credit card.
A list of employees who receive salary or wages, together with the amounts due to each.
A small document, included with an employee's wage or salary, giving details of money earned and tax and insurance paid.
(informal, computing) A system that restricts access to content with a purchase or a paid subscription.
The seventeenth letter of many Semitic alphabets/abjads (Phoenician, Aramaic, Hebrew פ, Syriac ܦ, and others; Arabic has the analog faa).

(especially, when without a qualifier) A plant, Pisum sativum, member of the legume (Fabaceae) family. Any of certain plants of the family Fabaceae: Pisum sativum and others. (culinary) The edible seed of various other pea plants. (baseball) A ball travelling at high velocity. (culinary) The edible seed of Pisum sativum.
A state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony. For instance, a state free from civil disturbance. Harmony in personal relations. A state free of war, in particular war between different countries.
The absence of mental turmoil or anxiety.
A tobacco pipe smoked ceremonially in certain Native American cultures that symbolizes peace among those who smoke it, and among whom it is passed around from person to person.
A series of formal discussions between two or more nation-states or groups of people held to resolve existing conflict between them.
An agreement to end fighting or conflict.
Favouring peace rather than conflict; not aggressive, tending to avoid violence (of people, actions etc.). [from 14th c.] Characterized by peace; peaceful, tranquil. [from 14th c.]
Not at war; not disturbed by strife or turmoil. Motionless and calm.
(politics) A situation where nation-states do not interfere with the domestic affairs of other countries, in order to avoid conflict; mutual non-interference.
In a peaceful manner.
The act of preserving peace, specifically between hostile groups or states, especially by a sanctioned military force. [from 17th c.]
A person who restores peace, especially by settling disputes; one who engages in peacemaking.
The period of time when a nation or people is at peace, not fighting a war.

(countable) Any tree of species Prunus persica, native to China and now widely cultivated throughout temperate regions, having pink flowers and edible fruit. (countable, uncountable) Soft juicy stone fruit of the peach tree, having yellow flesh, downy, red-tinted yellow skin, and a deeply sculptured pit or stone containing a single seed. (countable, informal) A particularly admirable or pleasing person or thing.
The flower of a peach tree that will eventually turn into a peach.
A South American palm tree with fleshy, edible fruit (Bactris gasipaes).
(informal) The soft, scanty beard of an adolescent male. (rare, nonstandard) The fuzz found on the skin of a peach.
A peafowl (of the genus Pavo or Afropavo), either male or female. (entomology) Any of various Asian species of papilionid butterflies of the genus Papilio.
A bird of the genus Pavo or Afropavo, notable for the extravagant tails of the males; a peacock (unspecified sex).

A point; the sharp end or top of anything that terminates in a point; as, the peak, or front, of a cap. The highest value reached by some quantity in a time period. (geography) The top, or one of the tops, of a hill, mountain, or range, ending in a point.
To rise or extend into a peak or point; to form, or appear as, a peak.
(medicine) An instrument that monitors the peak expiratory flow rate of air from a person's bronchi; used to manage asthma.
In the tourist industry, the period of highest demand.
A loud sound, or a succession of loud sounds, as of bells, thunder, cannon, shouts, laughter, of a multitude, etc.
A legume resembling a nut, the fruit of the plant Arachis hypogaea, native to South America.
A spread made from ground peanuts.
A milky liquid made from peanuts and used as a milk substitute.
(informal, figurative) Especially of a salary: a very insufficient or small amount.
(botany) The pod of the pea plant, that holds the seeds (the peas) until they ripen
A type of fruit tree (Pyrus communis).
A tree of the genus Pyrus, which bears the pears as fruits.
Having a shape of a (typical western) pear, or in cross-section, like the cross-section of a pear.

(literally) A shelly concretion, usually rounded, and having a brilliant luster, with varying tints, found in the mantle, or between the mantle and shell, of certain bivalve mollusks, especially in the pearl oysters and river mussels, and sometimes in certain univalves. It is usually due to a secretion of shelly substance around some irritating foreign particle. Its substance is the same as nacre, or mother-of-pearl. Round lustrous pearls are used in jewellery. (figuratively) Something precious. (uncountable, typography, printing, dated) The size of type between diamond and agate, standardized as 5-point.
Barley that has had the husk and bran removed.
A widely grown millet (Cenchrus americanus, syn. Pennisetum glaucum).
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see pearl,‎ necklace.
(idiomatic, often, sarcastic) A succinct, insightful saying, piece of advice, or moral precept.
Any of several bivalve molluscs that are a source of pearls, but especially Pinctada margaritifera.
Megastictus margaritatus, a passerine bird of the antbird family, native to South America.
(urology) A harmless hereditary anatomical variation consisting of small protuberances that may form on the ridge of the glans of the human penis.
(idiomatic) Teeth.

A member of the lowly social class that toils on the land, constituted by small farmers and tenants, sharecroppers, farmhands and other laborers on the land where they form the main labor force in agriculture and horticulture. A country person.
A female peasant.
(historical) Impoverished rural farm workers, either as serfs, small freeholders or hired hands.
(weaponry, slang) Any small or ineffective gun or weapon.
Soil formed of dead but not fully decayed plants found in bog areas, often burned as fuel. [from 14th c.]
A bog in which the soil is formed from peat.

A small stone, especially one rounded by the action of water.
(transitive) To pave with pebbles.
