details: A smooth, thin-shelled, edible oval nut of this tree.
A sweet pie made from corn syrup and pecans, considered a specialty of Southern United States cuisine.
A small flaw or sin.
Sinful.
Any of the family Tayassuidae of mammals from the Americas, related to pigs.

An act of striking with a beak. A small kiss.
To seize and pick up with the beak, or as if with the beak; to bite; to eat; often with up. To kiss briefly.
(colloquial, British) mildly hungry

(carbohydrate) A polysaccharide extracted from the cell walls of plants, especially of fruits; under acidic conditions it forms a gel. It is often used in processed foods, especially jellies and jams where it causes thickening (setting).
Resembling a comb.
(anatomy) Relating to, or connected with, the pubic bone.
(anatomy) A flat quadrangular muscle, situated at the anterior part of the upper and medial aspect of the thigh, whose primary function is hip flexion.
Of or pertaining to the breast, or chest.
(ichthyology) Either of two fins located on each side of a fish just behind the head.
Calidris melanotos, a small migratory wader that breeds in North America and Asia, wintering in South America and Oceania, and eats small invertebrates.
(medicine) A congenital deformity of the anterior wall of the chest, in which several ribs and the sternum grow abnormally, giving a caved or sunken appearance.
Out of the ordinary; odd; strange; unusual. Common or usual for a certain place or circumstance; specific or particular.
The quality or state of being peculiar; individuality; singularity. That which is peculiar; a special and distinctive characteristic or habit; particularity.
Of, or relating to, money; monetary, financial.
Of, or relating to pedagogy; teaching.
In a pedagogical manner, like a pedagogue.
A teacher or instructor of children; one whose occupation is to teach the young.
The profession of teaching. The activities of educating, teaching or instructing.

Of or relating to the foot.
A lever operated by one's foot that is used to control or power a machine or mechanism, such as a bicycle or piano.
To operate a pedal attached to a wheel in a continuous circular motion.
A push on the pedals.
(idiomatic) At maximum speed.
(UK, watercraft) A small boat propelled by pedals that directly turn external paddles, used for recreation.
A person who is overly concerned with formal rules and trivial points of learning.
Being overly concerned with formal rules and trivial points of learning, like a pedant. Tending to show off one’s knowledge, often in a tiresome manner.
An instance of such behaviour. An overly ambitious display of learning.
To sell things, especially door to door or in insignificant quantities. To sell illegal narcotics. (derogatory, figuratively) To spread or cause to spread.
An itinerant seller of small goods.
A man who is engaged in an erotic relationship with an adolescent boy; a practitioner of pederasty.
Relating to a man's erotic love for adolescent boys.
Erotic love, sexually expressed or chaste, between a man and an adolescent boy. (archaic) Anal intercourse in general, usually between a man and an adolescent boy.
(architecture) The base or foot of a column, statue, vase, lamp.

(not comparable) Of or intended for those who are walking.
A walker; one who walks or goes on foot, especially as opposed to one who uses a vehicle.
A place where pedestrians are permitted to or advised to cross a street.
The restriction of access to a street to pedestrians only.
(transitive) To restrict access to (a street) to pedestrians only, disallowing motor vehicles and sometimes cyclists
(American spelling) Of or pertaining to pediatrics, the branch of medicine dealing with the care and treatment of children and adolescents.
(American spelling) A physician that specializes in pediatrics; the medical care of infants, children, adolescents, and young adults.
(American spelling, medicine) The branch of medicine that deals with the treatment of children and adolescents.
A tricycle having a hooded cab to seat paying passengers.

(botany) A stalk of an individual flower (or fruit, e.g., once fertilised) or spore-producing body within a cluster. (mycology) A stalk of a fungus fruiting body. (anatomy) A stalk-shaped body part; an anatomical part that resembles a stem or stalk.
A cosmetic treatment for the feet and toenails.
A person who performs pedicures.
A chart, list, or record of ancestors, to show breeding, especially distinguished breeding. [from 15th c.]

(architectural element) A classical architectural element consisting of a triangular section or gable found above the horizontal superstructure (entablature) which lies immediately upon the columns; fronton.
(zootomy) Either of a second pair of appendages near the mouth of many arachnids, variously specialized as pincers, sensory or locomotory organs.
Of or pertaining to pedology (in all senses)

The sub-discipline of soil science that studies soils as a component of natural systems or deals with soil genesis and soil classification, or studies the soil profiles or solum in its natural setting. The study of the behaviour and development of children.
A device, often electronic, that measures the number of steps taken, and thus estimates the distance walked.

(psychiatry, sexology) An adult or older adolescent who is sexually attracted to prepubescent children. [from 20th c.] (pejorative, by extension, common use) An adult who is sexually attracted to or engages in sexual acts with a child under the age of consent.
Sexual attraction by adults and adolescents to children, specifically prepubescent children. (by extension, proscribed) Sexual activity between adults and children; the act of child molestation.
Of, relating to, or pertaining to pedophilia.
(botany) The stalk supporting an inflorescence or a solitary flower/fruit. (anatomy) A bundle of neurons connecting different parts of the brain.
Of or pertaining to a peduncle
Having a peduncle or stalk
The name of the Latin-script letter P/p.
(informal) To look slyly, or with the eyes half closed, or through a crevice; to peep. (informal) To be only slightly, partially visible, as if peering out from a hiding place.

(usually, uncountable) The skin or outer layer of a fruit, vegetable, etc. A shovel or similar instrument, now especially a pole with a flat disc at the end used for removing pizza or loaves of bread from a baker's oven.
(transitive) To remove the skin or outer covering of.
A household utensil for peeling fruit or vegetables.
The act of removing the outer surface in strips. Strips of an outer rind or surface that has been removed.

A short, soft, high-pitched sound, as made by a baby bird. A quick look or glimpse, especially a furtive one. A feeble utterance or complaint.
To make a soft, shrill noise like a baby bird. To speak briefly with a quiet voice. (intransitive, dated) To begin to appear; to look forth from concealment; to make the first appearance.
(colloquial, chiefly, in the plural) The eye.
A small hole, opening, or piece of glass, especially in a door, through which one can look without being seen.
A person who watches another without the other's permission and usually without the other's knowledge, especially for the purpose of deriving sexual pleasure from the sight of the other.

An exhibition of pictures or objects viewed through a small hole or magnifying glass. A titillating or pornographic display viewed through a small slot, generally equipped with a timer to automatically close the slot when payment has expired.

Somebody who is, or something that is, at a level or of a value equal (to that of something else). Someone who is approximately the same age (as someone else). A noble with a title, i.e., a peerage, and in times past, with certain rights and privileges not enjoyed by commoners.
(intransitive) To look with difficulty, or as if searching for something.
Inducement or influence by one's peers.

(education) The scholarly process whereby manuscripts intended to be published in an academic journal are reviewed by independent researchers (referees) to evaluate the contribution, i.e. the importance, novelty and accuracy of the manuscript's contents.
The rank or title of a peer or peeress.
Without peer or equal; unparalleled, nonpareil. Of the highest quality, best.

(colloquial) An annoyance or grievance.
(colloquial) To annoy; vex.
Constantly complaining, especially in a childish way due to insignificant matters; fretful, whiny.
The edible fruit of this plant, which has an orange or red skin when ripe, orange pulp which turns floury when cooked, and a single large seed.

A cylindrical wooden or metal object used to fasten or as a bearing between objects. A protrusion used to hang things on. One of the pins of a musical instrument, on which the strings are strained. (journalism) A topic of interest, such as an ongoing event or an anniversary, around which various features can be developed.
(transitive) To fix a value or price. (transitive, slang) To indicate or ascribe an attribute to.
A wooden leg, usually tapered, strapped onto the stump of an amputated leg.
(music, lutherie) The part of a violin or similar stringed instrument that holds the tuning pegs.

Disparaging, belittling or derogatory. [from 1882]
A disparaging, belittling, or derogatory word or expression.
In a pejorative manner. Insultingly, disparagingly; so as to belittle another or harm their reputation.
(biology) Living in the open sea rather than in coastal or inland waters.
Any of various seabirds of the family Pelecanidae, having a long bill with a distendable pouch.
(geology) A sedimentary rock containing very fine particles.
(pathology) A disease characterised by skin lesions and mental confusion, primarily caused by a niacin deficiency. [from 19th c.]

A small, compressed, hard chunk of matter. A lead projectile used as ammunition in rifled air guns. Compressed byproduct of digestion regurgitated by owls and many other birds of prey, which serves as a waste disposal mechanism for indigestible parts of food, such as fur and bones.
Pellitory of the wall (Parietaria officinalis). [from 15th c.]
Any of several plants having edible, pungent leaves or roots, especially Anacyclus pyrethrum.
Allowing the passage of light; translucent or transparent. Easily understood; clear.
Russian dumplings resembling ravioli.
(cycle racing) A group of riders formed during a cycling road race; especially, the main group of riders; the pack.

The skin of an animal with the hair or wool on; either a raw or undressed hide, or a skin preserved with the hair or wool on it (sometimes worn as a garment with minimal modification). (chiefly, Ireland, humorous, informal) Human skin, especially when bare; also, a person's hair.
To bombard (someone or something) with missiles. To force (someone or something) to move using blows or the throwing of missiles.
A dealer in pelts (animal skins).
Of, pertaining to, or in the region of, the pelvis
(ichthyology) Either of a pair of fins on either side and towards the rear of a fish.
(anatomy) A muscular partition, formed by the muscle fibers of the levator ani, the coccygeus, and associated connective tissue, which spans the area underneath the pelvis.
(anatomy) The large compound bone structure at the base of the spine that supports the legs in hominids.
(pathology) Any of a group of rare autoimmune blistering skin diseases that superficially resemble pemphigus.
(pathology) A severe autoimmune skin disease characterized by pustules and painful blisters, and which can be fatal.

An enclosure (enclosed area) used to contain domesticated animals, especially sheep or cattle. A tool, originally made from a feather but now usually a small tubular instrument, containing ink used to write or make marks. A female swan. (figurative) A writer, or their style.
(transitive) To write (an article, a book, etc.).
A fictitious name used by an author in place of their actual name; a writer's pseudonym.
A friend with whom one communicates using letters, usually over a long distance.
A colonial territory used (mainly) for the detention and forced labor of deportees, typically where free labor is desperately scarce.
(transitive) To subject to a penalty, especially for the infringement of a rule or regulation. (transitive, sports) To impose a handicap on.
According to a penal code
A legal sentence. (ice hockey) A punishment for an infraction of the rules, often in the form of being removed from play for a specified amount of time.
(soccer) A form of direct free kick, taken from the penalty spot after a defensive foul in the penalty box, with only the goalkeeper defending the goal.
(football, field hockey) A series of penalties (penalty kicks in soccer), taken to decide a winner after a game has resulted in a tie and extra time has been played.
(handball) A free throw taken by an attacker from 7 metres away, defended by the goalkeeper.

A voluntary self-imposed punishment for a sinful act or wrongdoing. It may be intended to serve as reparation for the act. A sacrament in some Christian churches that involves penitence (remorse plus restitution via prayer).
A writing utensil with a graphite (commonly referred to as lead) shaft, usually blended with clay, clad in wood, and sharpened to a taper. [from 16th c.]
An object purposed to contain different stationery like pencil, rubber, correction fluid, etc.
A small opened container for stationery such as pencils, ballpoint pens, rubber, correction fluid, etc.
The material (usually black or dark gray) which allows a pencil to work. Usually a mixture of graphite and smaller amounts of other material, but not actual lead.
(informal, often, derogatory) One who does routine office work; someone involved mainly in paperwork.
A device used to sharpen pencils by shaving the wood at one end.
A slim skirt (clothing) with a straight and narrow cut, usually approximately knee-length.
A tiny pencil (either manufactured that way, or become that way through constant usage).
Somewhat cylindrical and slender like a pencil; also, tall and thin.
A piece of jewellery which hangs down as an ornament, especially worn on a chain around the neck. [from 15th c.]
(also, attributive) A drop-shaped diamond or other gem used as a pendant; also, a piece of jewellery in pendant form. [from 19th c.]
(architecture) The concave triangular sections of vaulting that provide the transition between a dome and the square base on which it is set and transfer the weight of the dome.
Awaiting a conclusion or a confirmation. Begun but not completed.
Any of the family of small passerine birds Remizidae, which nearly all make nests which hang from trees; found in Eurasia, Africa, and North America.
(clocks, mechanics) A body suspended from a fixed support so that it swings freely back and forth under the influence of gravity, commonly used to regulate various devices such as clocks.
Any clock that uses a pendulum to regulate its movement.
Capable of being penetrated, entered, or pierced.
To enter into; to make way into the interior of; to pierce. To insert the penis into an orifice, such as a vagina, mouth, or anus.
A type of very low-viscosity oil that evaporates quickly.
The act of penetrating something. [from 15th c.]
(rare) Any of various porgies of the genus Calamus

Any of several flightless sea birds, of the family Spheniscidae within the order Sphenisciformes, found in the Southern Hemisphere, marked by their usual upright stance, walking on short legs, and (generally) their stark black and white plumage. [from 16th c.]

(biochemistry, pharmaceutical drug) A crystalline, sulfur-containing amino acid produced by the hydrolysis of penicillins, used pharmacologically as a chelating agent to remove heavy metals such as copper from the body, and as an anti-inflammatory agent, especially for rheumatoid arthritis; 2-amino-3-methyl-3-mercaptobutanoic acid, (CH3)2C(SH)CH(NH2)COOH.

(pharmaceutical drug) Any of a group of narrow-spectrum antibiotics obtained from Penicillium molds or synthesized, that have a beta-lactam structure and are active against gram-positive bacteria and used in the treatment of various infections and diseases.
Pertaining to the penis. [from 19th c.]
(geography) A piece of land projecting into water from a larger land mass.
Of, pertaining to, resembling, or connected with a peninsula or peninsulas.
(psychoanalysis) The unconscious desire of a woman to possess a penis.
A tubelike device placed over the penis to make it harder and larger, usually equipped with a hand pump or electric pump.
The condition of being penitent; a feeling of regret or remorse for doing wrong or sinning.
One under the direction of a confessor.
(chiefly, US) A state or federal prison for convicted felons; (broadly) a prison.
A flag normally used by naval vessels to represent a special condition.

(historical) In the United Kingdom and Ireland and many other countries, a unit of currency worth 1⁄240 of a pound sterling or Irish pound before decimalisation, or a copper coin worth this amount. Abbreviation: d.

Mentha pulegium, a plant of the mint family, formerly much used in various medicinal treatments and as a flea repellent.
Study of the processes devised and adopted for the punishment and prevention of crime.

A boarding house or small hotel, especially in continental Europe, which typically offers lodging and certain meals and services. [from 17th c.]
(finance) An annuity paid regularly as benefit due to a retired employee, serviceman etc. in consideration of past services, originally and chiefly by a government but also by various private pension schemes. [from 16th c.]
(transitive) To grant a pension to.
A pool of assets forming an independent legal entity that are bought with the contributions to a pension plan for the exclusive purpose of financing pension plan benefits.
Eligible to receive a pension.
(chiefly, UK, Canada) Someone who lives on a pension, especially the retirement or old age pension.
Engaged in, involving, or reflecting deep or serious thought. Having the appearance of deep, often melancholic, thinking.
In a thoughtful or reflective manner.
Repressed or suppressed, especially of emotions or impulses.
Five.
(mathematics) A four-dimensional object analogous to a tetrahedron, constructed out of five tetrahedra.
(geometry) A 50-sided polygon.
(geometry) A polygon with fifteen sides.
(organic compound) A potent, water-soluble high explosive, prepared by nitration of pentaerythritol.
Of, relating to, or shaped like a pentagon.

The shape of a five-pointed star constructed of five intersecting lines meeting at the vertices, such that a central pentagon and five surrounding isosceles triangles are formed; often with magical connotations; a 5/2 (or 5/3) star polygon.
(geometry) A polyhedron with five faces.
A set of five works of art that are connected, and that can be seen either as a single work or as five individual works.

(organic compound) An aliphatic hydrocarbon of chemical formula C5H12; either of the three isomers n-pentane, methylbutane (isopentane), and dimethylpropane (neopentane); volatile liquids under normal conditions.
(photography) A five-sided prism used in the viewfinder of most single-lens reflex cameras

(particle) Any of a class of subatomic particles (previously hypothetical, since detected, subject to confirmation) consisting of a group of five quarks (compared to three quarks in normal baryons and two in mesons), or more specifically four quarks and one antiquark (symbol Θ).
Having five syllables.
(athletics) An athlete who competes in the pentathlon.

(athletics) Ellipsis of modern pentathlon, a discipline with five events based on late-19th century basic military skills.
(music) Based on five tones.
(history, obsolete) A galley-type Grecian vessel with fifty oars.
